examples.en: The water purifier filters out impurities in the water.
If impurities get mixed into gold, its color turns dull.

examples.ko: 실험하기 전에 시료에서 불순물부터 없애야 해요.
examples.en: Before the experiment, you have to remove the impurities from the sample first.

examples.ko: 이 기름은 불순물 없이 맑아서 튀김에 좋아요.
examples.en: This oil is clear without any impurities, so it's good for frying.

examples.ko: 불순물이 많은 물은 그냥 마셔도 돼요?
examples.en: Is it okay to drink water that has a lot of impurities as it is?

examples.ko: 유리 속 불순물 때문에 빛이 이상하게 퍼져요.
examples.en: Because of the impurities inside the glass, the light spreads strangely.

explain: 쓰레기나 먼지와 달리, 원래 깨끗해야 할 물이나 금속, 기름에 섞여 들어간 다른 물질에 써요. 불순물이 없는 상태는 '순수하다', '순도가 높다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: Impurities got mixed into the water, so it tastes odd.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨끗해야 할 것에 다른 물질이 들어갔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something foreign got into what should be clean.

phrases.en: This machine removes impurities from oil.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 공정에서 깨끗하게 만든다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a machine or process purifies something.

phrases.en: This salt has no impurities.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순수하고 깨끗하다는 뜻으로 제품을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a product as pure and clean.

explain_en: Unlike trash or dust, this is used for other substances mixed into something that should be clean, such as water, metal or oil. A state without impurities is described as '순수하다' (pure) or '순도가 높다' (high purity).

examples.en: The cup fell on the floor and shattered to pieces.
My long-held dream was shattered in an instant.
I tore the paper to shreds and threw it in the trash.
The ship hit by the waves broke into pieces.
My trust collapsed completely because of his lie.
The petals were scattered in all directions by the wind.

explain: '깨지다', '부서지다', '찢어지다', '흩어지다'처럼 조각조각 나는 말과 같이 써요. 꿈, 희망, 믿음 같은 마음의 것이 무너질 때도 써요. 같은 뜻의 '산산조각이 나다'도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The window shattered to pieces.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산산이 깨지다'와 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 더 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 산산이 깨지다 and more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The petals scattered in every direction in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 조각이나 사람이 여기저기 멀리 퍼지는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes many pieces or people spreading far in all directions.

phrases.en: The letter was torn to shreds on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이나 천이 아주 작은 조각으로 찢어진 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes paper or cloth torn into very small pieces.

explain_en: Breaking or scattering into tiny pieces, also dreams or hopes (산산이 부서지다) It goes with verbs of breaking into pieces such as '깨지다', '부서지다', '찢어지다' and '흩어지다'. It is also used when abstract things like dreams, hopes and trust fall apart. The related phrase '산산조각이 나다' is also very common.

t90.ax: The ship hit by the waves broke into pieces.

examples.en: The road is blocked because of water and sewer work.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 상하수도가 넘칠 때가 있어요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, the sewer system sometimes overflows.

examples.ko: 시에서 낡은 상하수도를 새로 바꾸고 있어요.
examples.en: The city is replacing the old water and sewer lines.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 상하수도는 있는데 도시가스가 없어요.
examples.en: This village has water and sewage service but no city gas.
If there's a problem with the water or sewer, call city hall.

examples.ko: 상하수도와 전기가 끊겨서 하루 종일 불편했어요.
examples.en: The water, sewage and electricity were cut off, so it was a hassle all day.

explain: 깨끗한 물을 보내 주는 '상수도'와 쓴 물을 내보내는 '하수도'를 묶어서 부르는 말이에요. 주로 공사, 시설, 도시 기반 시설 이야기에서 나와요. 집 수도 요금은 보통 '수도 요금'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: They are doing water and sewage work in our neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길에서 하는 물 관련 공사를 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for street work on water systems.

phrases.en: They replaced the old water and sewage facilities with new ones.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도시의 기반 시설을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about city infrastructure.

phrases.en: Water supply and sewage do different jobs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 묶어 부르지 않고 둘을 나누어 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the two separately instead of together.

explain_en: It bundles '상수도' (the supply of clean water) and '하수도' (the drains that carry used water away). It mostly comes up in talk about construction, facilities and city infrastructure. For household bills, people usually just say '수도 요금'.

examples.en: They piled rice high on the plate for me.
I walked along a road deep with piled-up snow.

examples.ko: 집 앞에 쓰레기가 수북수북 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Garbage is piled high in front of the house.
I heaped tangerines into the basket.
The park with heaps of fallen leaves is pretty.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 서류가 수북수북 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Documents are piled high on the desk.

explain: '수북'을 되풀이한 말로, 소복하게 쌓인 모습을 더 생생하게 나타내요. 눈, 낙엽, 음식, 서류처럼 쌓이는 것에 어울려요.

phrases.en: Papers are piled high on the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수북수북'의 바탕이 되는 형용사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective that 수북수북 is based on.

phrases.en: Fallen leaves piled up on the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 되풀이하지 않고 한 번만 말하는 부사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form without repetition.

phrases.en: The snow has piled up deep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쌓이다'와 함께 쓰면 높이 쌓인 모습이 잘 나타나요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 쌓이다, it shows a high pile.

explain_en: It repeats '수북' and describes things piled up in heaps in a more vivid way. It suits things that pile up, such as snow, leaves, food or documents.

t90.ax: I heaped tangerines into the basket.

examples.en: It is a house with a roof made of tin sheet.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 양철 지붕에서 소리가 커요.
examples.en: When it rains, the tin roof gets loud.
I packed kimchi in a tin lunch box.
I watered the plants with a tin watering can.
Tin sheet rusts when it gets old.

examples.ko: 시골 창고 문이 양철이라 바람에 덜컹거려요.
examples.en: The door of the country shed is tin, so it rattles in the wind.

explain: '양철 지붕', '양철통', '양철 대문'처럼 옛날 시골 풍경 이야기에 자주 나와요. 비 오는 날 '양철 지붕에 떨어지는 빗소리'처럼 소리와 함께 떠올리는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 양철 지붕 위로 빗소리가 크게 들렸어요.
phrases.en: I could hear the rain loudly on the tin roof.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 시골집 이야기에 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, often found in stories about old country houses.

phrases.en: I collected water in a tin bucket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양철로 만든 통을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A container made of tinned iron.

phrases.en: The tin gate of the country house creaked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 집의 철로 된 대문을 떠올리게 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Evokes the metal gate of an old house.

explain_en: It often shows up in talk about old countryside scenes, as in '양철 지붕' (tin roof), '양철통' (tin bucket) or '양철 대문' (tin gate). People often link it with sound, like rain falling on a tin roof.

en: to be set up; to be embedded; to be installed

examples.en: A camera is installed at the building entrance.

examples.ko: 이 문은 자동으로 열리게 장치되어 있어요.
examples.en: This door is fitted to open automatically.
It is a room fitted with an alarm for safety.
No anti-theft alarm has been installed in the car.

examples.ko: 다리 아래에 감시 장비가 장치될 예정이에요.
examples.en: Monitoring equipment is scheduled to be installed under the bridge.

examples.ko: 벽 속에 비밀 스위치가 장치돼서 아무도 몰랐어요.
examples.en: A secret switch was built into the wall, so nobody knew.

explain: 일상에서는 '설치되다'가 훨씬 흔해요. '장치되다'는 기계나 장비를 어떤 목적에 맞게 갖춰 놓았다는 느낌이에요. 명사 '장치'는 자주 쓰지만 이 동사는 설명하는 글에서 가끔 나와요.

phrases.en: A new air conditioner was installed in the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장치되다'와 비슷한데 일상에서 훨씬 자주 써요. 말할 때는 이쪽이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 장치되다 but much more common in daily life, and more natural in speech.

phrases.example: 문 위에 장치된 카메라가 입구를 찍어요.
phrases.en: The camera set up above the door films the entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장치된' 뒤에 기계 이름을 붙여 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요. 설명하는 글에서 가끔 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a machine name after '장치된' to modify a noun; it appears occasionally in descriptive writing.

phrases.example: 이 방에는 경보기가 장치되어 있지 않아요.
phrases.en: There is no alarm installed in this room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 어떤 장비가 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says that some equipment is not set up.

explain_en: Passive; a device or sensor is fitted in (센서가 장치되다) '설치되다' is much more common in daily life. '장치되다' suggests equipment set up for a specific purpose. The noun '장치' is very common, but this verb only turns up now and then in explanatory writing.

t90.ax: This door is fitted to open automatically.

en: to be controlled (by a system); to be kept in check

examples.en: The temperature is controlled automatically.
The fire wasn't brought under control and spread.
This machine is run by a computer.
When emotions are kept in check, your speech softens.
You must run at a well-controlled speed.
I'm worried about whether the damage can be kept in check.

explain: 기계·온도·감정·상황이 정해진 범위 안에서 조절될 때 써요. 뉴스와 설명서에서 자주 나오고, 사람 사이에서 '통제하다'가 더 강한 느낌이에요. 컴퓨터 쪽에서는 '제어'가 기본 단어라서 '제어판', '원격 제어'처럼 많이 보여요.

phrases.en: The machine stopped because it could not be controlled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조절이 안 되고 마음대로 움직일 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used when something can't be kept under control.

phrases.en: The room temperature is adjusted automatically.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제어되다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than '제어되다' and more common in daily life.

phrases.en: The situation was brought under control before the fire spread.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제어되다'보다 강하게 눌러서 관리한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels stronger than '제어되다', as if held down firmly.

explain_en: Passive: a machine or system is controlled technically. For machines, temperature, emotions or situations being kept within a set range. Frequent in news and manuals; '통제하다' feels stronger between people. In computing '제어' is the standard word, as in '제어판' (control panel) and '원격 제어'.

dis.h: be kept in check, machine or system
gh: be adjusted to a suitable level
be restricted or closed off by authority
be pushed around by someone's whims

p.n: 조절되다 means adjusted to a level; 제어되다 means operated or kept under control.

t90.ax: This machine is run by a computer.

examples.en: I stacked the cake in layers and made it look pretty.
The books are placed on the shelves tier by tier.
Rice paddies spread out in terraces on the mountain slope.

examples.ko: 옷을 층층이 겹쳐 입으면 덜 추워요.
examples.en: If you wear clothes in layers, you feel less cold.
I packed the side dishes in the lunch box in layers.

examples.ko: 눈이 층층이 쌓여서 길이 안 보여요.
examples.en: The snow has piled up layer upon layer, so I can't see the road.

explain: '겹겹이'와 비슷하지만 '층층이'는 층이 나뉘어 쌓인 모양에 어울려요. '층층이 쌓다/쌓이다/놓다'처럼 자주 써요. 칸으로 나뉜 모양은 '칸칸이'를 써요.

phrases.en: I stacked the boxes in layers and moved them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 일부러 쌓을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person stacks things on purpose.

phrases.en: Snow piled up in layers on the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저절로 쌓일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things pile up naturally.

phrases.en: The plates are placed in tiers on the shelf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 층이 나뉜 곳에 물건이 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes items sitting on separate levels.

explain_en: Things stacked in floors or levels, like cakes or shelves. It is similar to '겹겹이', but '층층이' fits things stacked in distinct tiers. It is common in '층층이 쌓다/쌓이다/놓다'. For things divided into compartments, use '칸칸이'.

t90.ax: The books are placed on the shelves tier by tier.

examples.ko: 칼날이 무뎌서 야채가 잘 안 썰려요.
examples.en: The blade is dull, so vegetables do not cut well.
It is dangerous to touch the blade.

examples.ko: 새 칼날로 바꿨더니 종이가 잘 잘려요.
examples.en: After switching to a new blade, paper cuts well.
This blade is very sharp.
The child cut a hand on the blade.
The tip of the blade broke off.

explain: '칼'은 도구 전체이고 '칼날'은 자르는 얇은 부분이에요. 손잡이는 '칼자루'라고 해요. 날이 잘 들면 '날카롭다', 잘 안 들면 '무디다'를 써요.

phrases.en: This knife has a sharp blade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날이 잘 드는 칼을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a knife that cuts well.

phrases.en: The blade was dull, so I bought a new knife.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날이 잘 안 들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the blade doesn't cut well.

phrases.en: I cut my finger on the blade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 칼날 때문에 다쳤을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you get hurt by a blade.
phrases.en_equiv: to get cut by a blade

explain_en: '칼' is the whole knife and '칼날' is the thin cutting part. The handle is '칼자루'. A blade that cuts well is '날카롭다' (sharp); one that does not is '무디다' (dull).

en: to be torn down; to be demolished; to be pulled down

examples.en: The old house in my neighborhood was torn down.
This building will be demolished next year.
The school was torn down and an apartment complex went up.
It hurt to see the house being torn down.
The bridge was demolished, so we have to take a detour.
I heard the market building will be torn down soon.

explain: 헐리다는 건물이 누군가에 의해 무너지는 쪽에서 말하는 피동 표현이고, 건물을 허무는 쪽은 '헐다'나 '허물다'를 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '철거되다'가 더 흔하고, 헐리다는 오래된 집이나 추억 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The old buildings are being torn down one by one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물이 지금 헐리는 중일 때 '-고 있다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add -고 있다 when a building is being demolished right now.

phrases.en: The old building will be demolished soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헐리다와 뜻이 같고, 일상 대화에서는 '철거되다'가 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 헐리다, and more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: That house hasn't been torn down yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 그대로 남아 있을 때 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form for a building that is still standing.

explain_en: 헐리다 is the passive form, from the side of the building being taken down; the one doing it uses '헐다' or '허물다'. In everyday talk '철거되다' is more common, and 헐리다 appears often in stories of old houses and memories.

examples.en: Concentrated juice is drunk after mixing it with water.
A lot of water is lost during the concentration process.
I mixed the concentrate into warm water and drank it.
When the concentrating is done, the solution becomes much thicker.
Herbal medicine made by concentrating comes in a small amount.

examples.ko: 이 세제는 농축 제품이라 조금만 써도 돼요.
examples.en: This detergent is a concentrated product, so you only need a little.

explain: '농축 주스', '농축액', '농축 세제'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 자주 써요. 같은 뜻을 일상에서는 '진하게 하다'로 풀어 말해요. 동사로는 '농축하다', 저절로 되면 '농축되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I mix water into this concentrate and drink it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진하게 만든 액체를 가리키는 말이라 보통 물을 섞어 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a thickened liquid that you usually dilute with water.

phrases.en: They concentrate fruit juice to make juice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '농축'을 동사로 바꿔 사람이 진하게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, meaning a person makes something more concentrated.

phrases.en: With concentrated detergent, you only need a little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품 이름 앞에 붙여서 성분이 진하다는 것을 알려 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before product names to show the formula is concentrated.

explain_en: Making a liquid stronger by removing water (농축 주스) It is often placed before another noun, as in 농축 주스, 농축액 and 농축 세제. In daily speech people say '진하게 하다' for the same idea. The verbs are 농축하다 for doing it and 농축되다 for when it happens by itself.

examples.ko: 명태는 말리면 북어, 얼리면 동태가 돼요.
examples.en: Pollack becomes bugeo when dried and dongtae when frozen.
I bought one pollack at the market.
In winter, we make stew with pollack.
People make myeongnanjeot with pollack roe.
I'm picking out the fish meat to make pollack pancakes.
These days it's hard to find domestic pollack.

explain: 같은 명태라도 상태에 따라 이름이 달라요. 신선한 것은 '생태', 얼린 것은 '동태', 말린 것은 '북어'라고 해요. 그래서 찌개를 시킬 때는 '동태찌개', '북엇국'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I made frozen pollack stew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼린 명태를 '동태'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Frozen pollack is called 'dongtae'.

phrases.example: 북엇국은 속이 안 좋을 때 좋아요.
phrases.en: Dried pollack soup is good when your stomach is upset.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말린 명태를 '북어'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Dried pollack is called 'bugeo'.

phrases.en: In winter we eat fresh pollack stew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼리거나 말리지 않은 신선한 명태를 '생태'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fresh pollack, neither frozen nor dried, is called 'saengtae'.

explain_en: General name for the fish itself, fresh or in general use. The same fish has different names depending on its state: fresh is '생태', frozen is '동태' and dried is '북어'. That is why dishes are called things like '동태찌개' (frozen pollack stew) and '북엇국' (dried pollack soup).

en: to be created; to be formed

examples.ko: 파일을 저장하면 새 폴더가 자동으로 생성돼요.
examples.en: When you save the file, a new folder is created automatically.
This account was created yesterday afternoon.

examples.ko: 별은 가스와 먼지가 모여 생성되었다고 해요.
examples.en: They say stars were formed when gas and dust gathered together.
Please write down the newly generated password.

examples.ko: 문서가 생성되는 데 몇 초가 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a few seconds for the document to be generated.

examples.ko: 오류가 생성되지 않도록 순서대로 눌러 주세요.
examples.en: Please press them in order so that no error is generated.

explain: 컴퓨터와 과학 분야에서 특히 자주 써요. '파일이 생성되다', '계정이 생성되다'처럼 시스템이 자동으로 만들 때 어울려요. 사람이 손으로 만드는 건 '만들다'를 써요. '생성하다'가 능동, '생성되다'가 피동이에요.

phrases.en: When you save, the file is created automatically.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자동으로'와 함께 시스템이 알아서 만드는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 자동으로 it fits cases where a system creates something on its own.

phrases.en: The account hasn't been created yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만들어져야 하는데 아직 없다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that something expected has not been made yet.

phrases.en: A new folder was created.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '생성되다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday alternative to 생성되다.

explain_en: Passive: files, data or cells appear automatically. Common in computing and science. It fits cases where a system produces something automatically, as in '파일이 생성되다' or '계정이 생성되다'. For things people make by hand, use '만들다'. '생성하다' is active and '생성되다' is passive.

dis.h: comes into existence; files, data, cells

p.n: 창출되다 is for new value like jobs or profit, not for files.

t90.ax: This account was created yesterday afternoon.

examples.ko: 이 품종은 병에 강한 형질을 가지고 있어요.
examples.en: This variety has a trait that resists disease.
Twins resemble each other a lot in their inherited traits too.
The researchers selected only the superior traits and bred them.

examples.ko: 형질 중에는 환경에 따라 달라지는 것도 있어요.
examples.en: Among traits, some change depending on the environment.

examples.ko: 같은 부모에게서 태어나도 형질은 다를 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if born to the same parents, traits can differ.

examples.ko: 새로운 형질이 나타난 식물을 따로 관찰하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are observing separately the plants in which a new trait has appeared.

explain: 주로 생물 수업이나 유전 이야기에서 나오고, 눈 색이나 키, 병에 대한 저항성처럼 생물이 가진 특징을 말해요. '유전 형질', '우성 형질'처럼 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '특징'이나 '성질'이라고 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.example: 눈 색은 부모에게서 받은 유전 형질이에요.
phrases.en: Eye color is an inherited trait from your parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부모에게서 자식에게 전해지는 특징을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for features passed from parents to children.

phrases.en: Brown eyes are a dominant trait.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유전에서 겉으로 잘 드러나는 형질을 말하고, 생물 수업에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A trait that shows up strongly in heredity; common in biology class.

phrases.en: Children inherit traits from their parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물려받다'와 함께 쓰면 유전으로 받는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 물려받다 it means receiving traits through heredity.

explain_en: It mainly appears in biology classes and talk about genetics, referring to features of living things such as eye color, height or resistance to disease. It is often used as in '유전 형질' and '우성 형질'. In daily life people more often say '특징' or '성질'.
